newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta regulator bans trading in Bre-X stock.
newsitem.headline: Alberta regulator bans trading in Bre-X stock.

text.p: The Alberta Securities Commission on Thursday slapped a cease-trade order on shares of disgraced gold explorer Bre-X Minerals Ltd and sister company Bro-X Minerals Ltd for failing to file financial statements.

The order means shares in the Calgary-based companies, which were delisted on three North American exchanges after Bre-X's Busang gold property in Indonesia was deemed to be a major fraud, cannot be bought or sold in Alberta -- even in the over-the-counter market.

Bre-X said last week it would not be able to release year-end financial statements in time to meet the commission's guidelines. The companies have not released audited financial statements since last December.
An interim cease-trade order on the shares was already in place in Alberta.
Company officials and its lawyers did not attend the hearing to contest the trading ban.
Commission chairman Bill Hess told reporters that other securities regulators, including the Ontario Securities Commission, had temporary bans in place and those would also likely be extended.

Bre-X and its sister companies have filed for creditor protection in the wake of a stunning report earlier this month that said the Busang property, once touted as the gold find of the century, was worthless and a fraud.

While Thursday's hearing was just to ban trading in Bre-X shares for failure to release financial data, investigations into other possible securities violations involving the company would continue, Hess said.
"There are a number of issues relating to disclosure and insider trading we're looking at," he said.
Hess said he could not comment on specific details of the probe, including how long it was expected to take.
"Investigations are very complicated. There's a lot of paper work, analysis of trading, computer record, things like that. They do take a long time," he said.
